Do you guys keep a gardening journal? May I see it?

I take lots of notes but I've found that over time, they tend to get lost.

Occasionally, I copy thoughts/ideas/discoveries I want to save into documents in my google drive folder where I know I can find them. I've had much better luck finding things there. Sorting things later helps me know what is worth keeping long term.

Relatively recently I've started writing the date on plant tags and throwing them in my seed saving box so I can find them later. I've got a bunch of daylilies and other plants I wish I knew the variety name to but don't because I lost the tag, notes, or receipt that I didn't file them in a way that I could find years later.

I also keep a list of things I want to grow soon on Google Keep because it is so easily accessible. Anything I want to keep a permanent record of though, goes on Drive.

I used to keep a handwritten one, but it became too much effort. Now, I take photos....lots and lots of photos. I have even started taking photos of the tags on new plants since I also tend to lose them. So my journal is a whole pile of albums on my iPad.

To keep track of the varieties, I keep a spreadsheet that includes the place they were bought (when I'm feeling energetic) and where they sit in the yard. That last part can be hit and miss based on whether I remember that I relocated something. This tends to be a winter chore, along with my attempt to draw them on a map. That's where the pictures come in handy...in the middle of winter, I can remember what was where. However, the map is definitely never up to date...it's just a mid-winter release for my gardening drive.

And my list of things to buy or ideas for future sit on my phone on a note pad type app. I also have a beer list, wine list, distillery list and grocery list. Haha!

I can't really share the spreadsheet and have too many pics to upload....but these are some ideas for you!

I started keeping one this year and so far it's awesome. What variety of mustard did I plant? How long did it take for the peas to mature? How much garlic did I harvest (not enough). I can't wait to look back next year and to have all this recorded info to improve upon.Here's my journal with one random page I try to write down everything that happens, which seeds were planted and where, when they popped, when they matured, when and how much I fed them, pests/ pest control, when wild fruits in the area mature, and also recording the recipes I use for canning.

I grew up planting and digging, and having big gardens and all that. I dunno, I just seem to remember it all well. I keep seeds and mark them, that sort of thing, but as far as a log and a written down book.. never have felt the want or need.
